verdict.headline: Iran says two tankers hit mines in Hormuz as markets wait on Meta and Tesla results
verdict.label: Saturday night: no session. S&P 500 closed Fri at 7,659.44 (-1.09%, week -1.9%), seven points under 7,666.45; Nasdaq 26,140.03 (week -4.5%); Dow 52,002.41 (week +0.7%); VIX ~20; 10Y ~5.085%; Brent $109.86 Fri; BTC ~$81,509 (flat 24h).
verdict.horizon: Sunday evening's oil and futures open through Wednesday October 21, when Tesla, Meta and Texas Instruments report
verdict.rationale_short:
What happened: no stock, bond or oil market has traded since Friday's close, when the S&P 500 finished at 7,659.44, seven points below the 7,666.45 level recent reports named as the sign of selling spreading beyond AI, after the chip index's eighth straight loss. On Saturday Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two oil tankers carrying about 2 million barrels of crude each caught fire after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz. That claim is not independently confirmed: US Central Command says it has cleared the strait of mines and that ships are being hit by projectiles instead. Either way, ships are still being struck, with four tankers reported hit since Friday. Bitcoin, the only market trading, was near $81,509 on Saturday night, almost unchanged over 24 hours and about $1,200 above its $80,320 low.

What it means: the weekend added oil risk, not new information about the AI selling that drove the week. Brent settled Friday at $109.86 after touching $110, and these attacks happened after that price was set, so oil's Sunday evening open is the first market to price them. The two accounts disagree on how the ships were hit, and the difference matters: mines would be harder and slower to clear than projectile attacks. Neither side's account has been independently verified, so the size of any oil move is uncertain. Bitcoin's flat weekend says nothing about whether the stock selling continues; it did not join Friday's decline either.

What would change the picture: an oil settle above $110 would add to the inflation pressure that keeps a Fed hike in play ahead of the October 27-28 meeting, while a fade back toward $104.7 would ease it. For stocks, a close back above 7,666.45 early in the week would make Friday look like an options-expiry overshoot; a second close below it with the Dow down more than 1% would show the selling spreading past AI. Netflix reports Tuesday, and Tesla, Meta and Texas Instruments on Wednesday. Meta's capital spending plans and Texas Instruments' demand outlook are the first direct reads on whether chip prices reflect a real slowdown. Conviction is low because markets are closed and this run could only check sources through search results, not by reading the articles in full.
verdict.lede_short: Iran says two tankers hit mines in Hormuz on Saturday; the US says it cleared the mines and ships are being hit by projectiles. Either way, attacks continued after oil settled near $110 on Friday, so Sunday's oil open is the first price on them. For stocks the weekend changed little: the S&P 500 sits just under 7,666, and results from Meta and Texas Instruments on Wednesday are the next real test of the chip selling.
